planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container transplants in spring or fall in full sun, well-drained soil; Barbeque is an upright rosemary cultivar selected for long, strong, straight woody stems well suited to stripping and using as flavorful skewers for grilling, in addition to standard culinary use.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, slightly alkaline soil; rosemary tolerates poor, rocky, sandy soils far better than rich garden soil, which promotes lush but frost-tender growth. Barbeque is an upright, vigorous rosemary cultivar selected specifically for producing long, strong, straight woody stems, prized by cooks for stripping the needles and using the stem itself as an aromatic skewer for grilling meat, seafood, or vegetables, infusing the food with rosemary flavor as it cooks. Beyond its skewer use, it is a fully capable culinary rosemary with the classic piney, resinous fragrance and flavor, and its upright, well-branched habit also makes an attractive hedge or specimen shrub. Like other rosemary cultivars, it thrives on relative neglect once established, needing little water or fertilizer, and is more prone to root rot from overwatering than from drought. Prune lightly after flowering to maintain a tidy shape and to harvest a fresh supply of long, straight stems for skewers.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container transplants in spring or fall in full sun, well-drained soil; Gorizia is an Italian heirloom rosemary cultivar prized for unusually large leaves and a milder, less resinous flavor than standard rosemary, along with strong, upright, vigorous growth.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, slightly alkaline soil. Gorizia is an heirloom Italian rosemary cultivar, named for the city in northeastern Italy, valued for producing notably larger leaves than standard rosemary along with a milder, sweeter, less resinous flavor that many cooks find more versatile in the kitchen since it is less likely to overpower a dish. It grows into a large, vigorous, upright shrub, often taller and more substantial than typical rosemary cultivars, making it a good choice as a specimen shrub, informal hedge, or the backbone of a culinary herb bed where its size and productivity provide a generous, continuous harvest. Like other rosemary, it thrives in lean, well-drained, slightly alkaline soil and struggles in heavy clay or soil that stays wet, so raised beds or berms are useful in areas with poor drainage. It is somewhat less cold-hardy than selections like Arp and performs best in zone 8-10, where it can remain evergreen and productive year-round. Prune after flowering to maintain shape and encourage bushy new growth for continued harvest.
sources: American Herb Society — Rosemary Variety Selection

common_name: Spice Islands Rosemary (Classic Strongly Flavored Culinary Rosemary)

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container transplants in spring or fall in full sun, well-drained soil; Spice Islands is a classic, widely grown culinary rosemary cultivar valued for strong, pungent, traditional rosemary flavor and consistent, easy-to-maintain upright growth.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, slightly alkaline soil. Spice Islands is a long-established culinary rosemary cultivar bred for strong, classic, pungently resinous rosemary flavor and fragrance, considered one of the most reliably flavorful rosemary cultivars for everyday cooking use. It grows into a dense, upright, well-branched shrub with the typical narrow, needle-like, dark green leaves and pale blue flowers of standard rosemary, making it equally useful as a culinary herb, an evergreen landscape shrub, or a low informal hedge. Like other rosemary, it thrives in lean, sharply drained, slightly alkaline soil and full sun, and is far more likely to suffer from overwatering and poor drainage than from drought or neglect. Harvest sprigs anytime for fresh use, or cut and dry larger quantities for winter storage. Prune lightly after flowering, or anytime during the growing season when harvesting, to maintain a full, bushy shape and encourage continued tender new growth.
sources: American Herb Society — Rosemary Variety Selection

planting.note: Root stem cuttings or plant container specimens in sharply drained, alkaline to neutral, poor to average soil in full sun; Creeping Red Thyme forms a dense, low mat covered in vivid magenta-crimson flowers in late spring and early summer, among the most colorful of the low groundcover thymes.

directions: Root stem cuttings or plant container specimens in sharply drained, alkaline to neutral, poor to average soil in full sun. Creeping Red Thyme forms a very low, dense mat of tiny, dark green leaves that disappears almost entirely beneath a vivid carpet of magenta-crimson flowers in late spring and early summer, among the showiest bloom displays of any low-growing groundcover thyme and a strong draw for bees. It tolerates light foot traffic once established, making it useful between stepping stones, along the edges of dry paths, and cascading over rock walls, and it spreads steadily to fill gaps without becoming aggressive or weedy. Like other creeping thymes, it is grown primarily for ornamental groundcover use and pollinator value rather than culinary purposes, and it thrives in the same lean, sharply drained, sun-baked conditions that stress most other groundcovers, making it valuable for hot, dry sites such as gravel gardens and rock gardens. Shear lightly after flowering to keep the mat dense and encourage fresh new growth.
sources: Missouri Botanical Garden Plant Finder — Thymus praecox Cultivars
North Carolina State Extension — Groundcover Thyme Selection

common_name: Lemon Frost Thyme (Variegated Lemon-Scented Groundcover Thyme)

planting.note: Root stem cuttings or plant container specimens in sharply drained, alkaline to neutral, poor to average soil in full sun; Lemon Frost combines finely variegated, cream-edged foliage with a strong lemon fragrance, providing both ornamental interest and culinary use as a low, spreading thyme.

directions: Root stem cuttings or plant container specimens in sharply drained, alkaline to neutral, poor to average soil in full sun. Lemon Frost is a variegated selection of lemon thyme, its small, gray-green leaves edged in creamy white for a frosted, two-tone effect that stands out clearly against plain green groundcovers and adds brightness to a rock garden or herb bed even before it flowers. Crushed foliage releases a strong, clean lemon fragrance along with the characteristic thyme aroma, and the leaves are fully usable in the kitchen anywhere a citrusy thyme flavor is wanted, from roasted chicken to herbal tea. Small pale lavender-pink flowers appear in early summer and attract bees, though the foliage color and fragrance remain the plant's main appeal through the rest of the season. Like other creeping thymes, it thrives in lean, sharply drained soil in full sun and struggles in rich, moist, or poorly drained conditions, which promote rot and reduce the intensity of both flavor and fragrance. Shear lightly after flowering to maintain a dense, tidy mat and encourage fresh, brightly variegated new growth.
sources: Missouri Botanical Garden Plant Finder — Thymus x citriodorus Cultivars
